outcomes: A service publishes and handles typed envelopes across memory, local, provider, or managed transports
A handler can choose competing or broadcast delivery and bound its concurrency and queue
Transient failures retry with stable message identity while permanent or exhausted failures have an explicit terminal outcome
Operators can distinguish handled, retried, dead-lettered, and dropped messages
nonGoals: Guaranteeing exactly-once delivery or globally ordered topics
Treating a dedupe key as framework-managed deduplication state
Falling back or dual-publishing after an ambiguous managed publish outcome

requirements.text: Competing handlers select one matching consumer while broadcast handlers select every matching consumer; retries and provider redelivery mean handlers must tolerate duplicates.
A handler invocation is deadline-bound, retries use bounded exponential backoff with stable event identity, and a retry for one Redis consumer group is not amplified into another group.
After retry exhaustion a message is reported dead-lettered only after a DLQ subscriber accepts it; otherwise it is reported dropped, never both.
Broker shutdown rejects new publishes, cancels pending retry timers, drains counted in-flight deliveries up to the configured deadline, and never invokes a retry after Stop returns.
Provider ingress strips caller-supplied auth attributes and push delivery authenticates and allowlists the pusher before invoking a handler.

With events.transport set to pubsub and no factory registered for it, the plugin publishes through the built-in Google Cloud Pub/Sub transport with Application Default Credentials. Each envelope becomes one message: the JSON envelope as data, its attributes, and its key as ordering key. A failed publish is retryable for 429 and 503 answers or a missing access token, permanent for other 4xx answers except 408, 409 and 499 or a malformed token, and ambiguous otherwise.

Under push delivery the plugin mounts its receiver on the application's single server when the application configures, after it resolves the events config, and mounts it once however often the application configures. A push application that holds no server, or several, fails configure with an error that names RegisterOn. RegisterOn chooses the server and is never repeated. Pull and stream delivery need no server and mount no receiver.
